course.title: Climate & Architectural Design
course.exam: Answer 3 sets from each section out of 4.

sets.title: Thermal Comfort, Heat Exchange & Comfort Indices
sets.desc: Most stable Section A family: comfort, heat exchange, heat loss, regulation and comfort indices.

sets.title: Ventilation, Air-space, Infiltration & Numericals
sets.desc: Strongest recent numerical trend: ACH, heat loss, fire shelter and laboratory ventilation.

sets.title: Microclimate, Envelope, Airflow & Shading
sets.desc: Sketch-heavy design set covering spacing, openings, envelope response and solar shading.

sets.title: Climate, Context & Climate-friendly Construction
sets.desc: Climate-context-comfort, KHANA/Vitruvius, green/sustainable ideas and climate-friendly construction.

sets.title: Global Climatic Factors, Earth-Sun Relation & Wind System
sets.desc: Radiation, Earth-Sun geometry, thermal balance, global winds, Coriolis and ITCZ.

sets.title: Tropical Climate Classification & Design Response
sets.desc: Warm-humid, hot-dry and composite climate characteristics with design responses.

sets.title: Regional, Site & Urban Climate
sets.desc: Macro/site/micro climate, local modifiers, site analysis and urban heat-island effects.

sets.title: Elements, Measurement, DRI & Basic Thermal Response
sets.desc: Temperature, humidity, precipitation, wind, DRI, wind rose and climatic measurement.

sectionA: Condition → Circumstance → Consequence; climate, context, comfort and man-made environment.
Climate & Built Environment: Vitruvius and KHANA
Ancient climate-responsive ideas, Bengali vernacular site zoning and mitigation logic.
T-R-H-A comfort factors, heat balance and four exchange paths.
External/internal environmental responsibilities and climate-design knowledge base.
ET, CET, EW, OT, solar incidence, atmospheric depletion and RH.
Climate hierarchy, local modifiers, measurement and site assessment.
Layout, spacing, openings, air movement and enclosure for different climates.
Envelope response of roof, floor, wall, windows, balconies and overhangs.
Horizontal, vertical and combined shading; external shading is most effective.
Tube house, rat-trap bond, green vs sustainable building and climate-conscious materials.
Air-space, infiltration, ACH, fresh-air table, heat-loss numericals and safety checks.
sectionB: Fit building to climate: comfort, energy saving, protection and natural resource use.
Solar radiation, Earth-Sun relation, thermal balance, winds, Coriolis, ITCZ and topography.
Temperature, humidity, vapour pressure, precipitation and measurements.
Driving rain, sky condition, solar duration/intensity, wind measurement and wind rose.
Warm-humid, hot-dry, composite/monsoon and associated climatic characteristics.
Macro/site/micro climate, deviation factors and urban climate.
Metabolism, heat gain/loss, thermal balance, vasomotor adjustment and comfort variables.

formulas.name: Relative Humidity
formulas.hint: AH = actual/absolute humidity; SH = saturation humidity at the same temperature.

formulas.name: Atmospheric Pressure
formulas.hint: Total pressure = dry-air partial pressure + vapour partial pressure.

formulas.name: Cosine Law
formulas.hint: β is measured from the surface normal. Normal incidence gives maximum intensity.

formulas.name: Driving Rain Index
formulas.hint: R in m and wind speed in m/s → DRI in m²/s.

formulas.name: Human Heat Balance
formulas.hint: Steady deep-body temperature means net heat storage is approximately zero.

formulas.name: Total Fresh-air Requirement
formulas.hint: Multiply occupants by required fresh-air supply per person.

formulas.name: Air Changes per Hour
formulas.hint: Q in m³/s and room volume V in m³.

formulas.name: Heat Loss due to Air Change
formulas.hint: Use SI units; n = air changes/hour.
